## What the prompt fix costs (v1 → v3, shipped)

v3 leaves the system prompt **byte-identical to v1** and adds a short dietary reminder next to the question, **only when the question states a dairy restriction**:
**+421 characters ≈ +105 input tokens** (≈4 chars/token — an *estimate*).

| | per query | this request | across the week of logs |
|---|---|---|---|
| v1 (before) | $0.00011587 | $0.00011587 | mean $0.00011774 |
| **v3 (shipped)** | +$0.00000787 on restricted questions only | **≈ $0.00012375** (+6.8%) | mean ≈ $0.00012073 (+2.53% — only 37.9% of queries state a restriction) |
| v2 (tried, rejected) | +114 tok on **every** query ≈ +$0.00000855 | ≈ $0.00012442 (+7.4%) | mean ≈ +7.3% |

So the shipped fix costs about **$0.0000079 extra on the queries that need it** — effectively free on average.
*Caveat:* the 38% restricted share is an artefact of the simulated log (half of the real pool I resampled from were deliberately dietary probes); real traffic would have far fewer, so the true average bump is **below** the figure in the table. (Prompt caching of the static system prompt would shave the baseline too — not turned on.)

> I deliberately did **not** optimise anything this week before attributing cost by stage (the "common mistake" in the brief):
> the stage table above is the attribution; the only change made to cost is the +105-token conditional reminder, and its effect is stated above.
